label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's the email — firm, factual and chronological, so it reads like a teacher keeping a record rather than someone venting. It stays polite throughout but makes the deadline and the consequences very clear.

---

**Subject:** Order TH-48217 — delivery not received (proof of delivery doesn't match) — resend or full refund needed by 13 Nov

Dear Tiny Hands Edu Supplies Customer Service,

I'm writing about order **TH-48217**, placed on **21 October**, for **R1,640 including R95 delivery**, paid by card.

Your tracking tells me it was delivered on **Tuesday 3 November at 11:42**, signed for by **"M. Adams"**. Nothing arrived.

I'm writing to you and not to the courier because my contract is with Tiny Hands. I never chose who delivers my orders, and being passed between you and a courier partner isn't going to get my finger paint back in time for my class.

**What the delivery claim doesn't match up**

- There is no staff member called Adams at Bergview Pre-Primary in Plumstead. The address on my order is correct.
- Our gate guard, Uncle Faizel, signs for and records every delivery in a book. There is no entry for 3 November.
- The items in the order are: 6 tubs of finger paint, 4 bags of playdough, 200 paper plates, googly eyes, glitter glue and 2 rolls of brown paper. None of it came.

**What I've already done**

- Emailed on **4 November** and **6 November**. Both times I received the same copy-and-paste reply saying you "have escalated my query to our courier partner".
- Phoned on **Friday**: 38 minutes on hold, and I was told nothing can be done until the courier's investigation is finished, which could take **10 working days**.

**Why the timing matters**

My class made their masks last week, and I've spent a week telling them the paint is "coming soon". The end-of-year concert is on **27 November** and I need these supplies for the props. Every working day I wait is another day of making promises to five-year-olds that I can't keep.

**What I'm asking for — by Friday 13 November, one of the following:**

1. **A re-send** of order TH-48217 to the same Bergview Pre-Primary address, with the tracking reference sent to me directly; or
2. **A full refund of R1,640, including the R95 delivery fee**, back to the card I paid with.

I'd also like someone to **reply to me directly** rather than send another template. A named contact and a direct email or phone number would help — but what I really want is a clear human answer to two questions: *was this delivered or not, and what happens next?* I've now had the same escalation sentence three times without a single concrete update.

For the record, I have ordered from Tiny Hands three times before with no issues at all, which is exactly why this one is so frustrating. I'm a kindergarten teacher on a teacher's salary, and this is money I paid myself for materials for other people's children. I can't absorb R1,640 out of my own pocket and I can't keep chasing this in my spare time.

If I don't receive a resolution by **Friday 13 November**, I will dispute the payment with my bank and leave an honest review. I'd much rather carry on using you — but I need this closed out one way or the other.

Kind regards,
[Your full name]
Kindergarten Teacher
Bergview Pre-Primary, Plumstead, Cape Town
[Your phone number]
[Your email address]

---

**Two practical tips before you send it:**
- Attach your card payment confirmation and the screenshots of both template replies — it removes any argument about whether the order was paid for or how many times you've contacted them.
- If you do get a call back, ask for the name of the person handling it and note the date and time. If they say "escalated" again, ask what the *actual next step* is and by when — that's usually where it unravels.
